entries.final_answer: In: make the named nightly nodes of #7177, #7178, #7111, #7181, #7182, #7183 pass again via brownfield point cuts in the files the debrief names, plus a changelog fragment and the Mission dossier. Out: refactors, src changes beyond the #7178 renderer, new gates, weakening or deleting any guard, running full suites, push/PR (the independent reviewer owns review and landing).
entries.question: What is in scope, and what is explicitly out?

entries.final_answer: Primary actor: the maintainer reading the nightly. Done: every named failing node id passes locally, each re-pin is at least as strong as before for the behaviour it guards and cites its contract-change commit, the git-remedies gate stays at an empty allowlist, and #7178 is fixed in production code with byte-identical notice output.
entries.question: Who is the primary actor and what outcome counts as done?

entries.final_answer: A test is never weakened to green (no subset or negation assertions, no deleting a pin without a stronger home); the git-remedies gate allowlist stays empty; checkout_file_recipe, not restore_recipe, renders the file-restore remedy because restore_recipe would drop the staged edit kept by the staged_differs branch (5b822c28ca) and fails for index_only; the #6754 seed-actor guard stays; charter interview keeps its own _emit_error JSON shape, distinct from charter status typed envelope.
entries.question: What must always hold, and which test changes are forbidden?

entries.final_answer: Run the exact failing node ids locally before (RED) and after (GREEN), then the owning test files and named gates (test_git_remedies, test_read_tracked_meta_6673, test_destructive_op_routing, test_caller_seed_refusal_6754, test_status_broken_charter_6557, etc.); ruff check and ruff format --check --force-exclude on touched files; no full suites (NO_FULL_HEAVY_SUITES_IN_MISSION). Record commands and counts.
entries.question: How is each fix verified, given the nodes are nightly-only in CI?

entries.final_answer: Mission (never Feature); name the sense of overloaded terms (primary, merge, routing, residue); 'residue' here is the read-side not-selectable-mission-dir sense (#5875); 'sync' is not used. Cite contract-change commits as in the debrief.
entries.question: Which terms are canonical and what must be avoided?

entries.final_answer: Four independent WPs on one branch, run sequentially (single_branch has no lanes): WP01 #7177 + #7111 (test re-pins); WP02 #7178 (the only production change, checkout_file_recipe in _git_remedies.py plus its unit tests); WP03 #7181 + #7182 (charter tests); WP04 #7183 (five independent point cuts, six nodes). WP01 first as the cheapest; no dependencies between WPs; changelog fragment and follow-up note land in WP04.
entries.question: How are the 19 nodes split into work packages, and in what order?

entries.final_answer: Before editing, each WP runs its exact node ids on the current tree and records the failure; after the edit it re-runs the same ids plus the owning files and named gates. Counts go in the WP's commit message and the final report. Strength-preservation is spot-checked by temporarily reverting one guarded behaviour where cheap (not committed).
